chunks: Verily the lightning could snatch away their eyes. When it flashes forth they walk in its flare. When darkness returns they stand still. And if the Lord wills so He could take away their hearing and sight; surely God is all-powerful.
ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor of lightning and darkness used to describe in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as describing the hypocrites' reliance on external, fleeting signs of faith rather than internal conviction, leaving them vulnerable to spiritual blindness when divine guidance is withdrawn. The imagery of lightning (*barq*) symbolizes the intermittent illumination of their hearts, which is insufficient for steady progress, highlighting the fragility of their belief compared to the steadfastness of the true believers. This condition serves as a warning that God’s power to remove their faculties is absolute, emphasizing the consequence of their duality in action and intent.
